channel.description: A permanent record of Polyemergence coverage across AI and emerging technology, organized by Singapore publication date.

item.title: Google brings Duplex AI calling to the Gemini app
item.description:
According to Google Research:
According to Google, the architecture behind its conversational calling features has evolved through three distinct phases over the past ten years. In the pre-LLM era, the system relied on task-specific recurrent neural networks constrained to narrow domains like restaurant bookings. As generative models emerged, Google employed hybrid stacks combining LaMDA with deterministic guardrails. Today, the latest stack uses Gemini foundation models to handle unbounded, multi-constraint tasks without rigid task-specific training.
Google reports that live telephony introduces unique technical hurdles, including pragmatic grounding to understand how conversations unfold with busy merchants and maintaining sub-second latency despite loud acoustic backgrounds like kitchen clatter and street noise. To address this, the system incorporates custom acoustic models and conversation cadence handling.
To ensure responsible use, Google states that every automated call clearly discloses that it is an AI agent, and businesses retain the ability to opt out through their Google Business Profile or by requesting the agent to stop during a call. Powered by newer models including Gemini 4 Hydrogen and Gemini 4 Neon, the updated system can now support complex workflows such as processing secure transactions via the Agent Payments Protocol and coordinating across email and RCS.

item.title: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod adds managed cluster extensions for Slurm
item.description: According to AWS Machine Learning: Maintaining a shared Slurm cluster for foundation model development has traditionally required synchronizing multiple configuration files, custom scripts, and user rosters across nodes. To address configuration drift, Amazon SageMaker HyperPod has expanded its declarative management approach to running nodes. The newly launched cluster extensions currently support two main capabilities: an observability extension that collects metrics for CloudWatch or Prometheus, and a user management extension that handles local accounts, Active Directory integration, SSH access, and Slurm accounting. These extensions are validated up front against schemas, applied consistently to all nodes including newly scaled or replaced instances, and provide detailed health monitoring without requiring fleet-wide script updates.

item.title: Curiosity Spots Drifting Twilight Clouds on Mars
item.description: According to NASA News: NASA reports that the Curiosity Mars rover captured images of drifting clouds on October 31, 2026, marking the 5,061st Martian day of its mission. Using its navigation cameras, the rover documented these post-sunset clouds, known as twilight clouds, which typically emerge for brief periods every fall within Gale Crater. Curiosity has been investigating this region for more than 14 years. The mission is managed for NASA by the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, built by JPL and overseen by Caltech in Pasadena, California, as part of the Mars Exploration Program.

item.title: Researcher plants 2 million canaries in AI supply chain and exposes major privacy leaks
item.description: As reported by Ars Technica, security researcher HD Moore conducted an experiment by sending nearly two million AI prompts containing unique, trackable secrets—such as AWS access keys and private git references—through various AI routers and inference services. The findings show that the complex AI supply chain leaks sensitive data heavily. Specifically, at least three AI hosting providers were compromised by attackers who stole AWS keys right at the provider's front door, even when requests were rejected before running a model. Furthermore, some inference resellers logged and passed along prompts to unauthorized parties, while certain AI labs scraped secret URLs embedded in prompts despite explicit 'zero data retention' policies. Moore suggests that using on-premises servers or dealing directly with first-tier providers can minimize risks, though complete privacy remains extremely difficult to guarantee in the current AI ecosystem.

item.title: New approach enables physically consistent AI models of chaotic systems
item.description: According to MIT Advanced Manufacturing: Background Predicting complex and chaotic systems like weather patterns, ocean currents, and turbulent flows is notoriously difficult. While artificial intelligence models can learn from data, they often suffer from a fundamental flaw: small initial errors accumulate over time, causing simulations to drift into physically impossible states where values grow without limit. Details According to MIT researchers Sunbochen Tang, Navid Azizan, and Themistoklis Sapsis, previous attempts relied on soft penalties during training, which offered no guarantee at test time. The team’s new approach introduces a projection layer that enforces hard constraints based on real-world energy dissipation. The model learns an energy-like function and a confinement boundary, ensuring that predictions remain bounded over arbitrarily long forecast windows while still preserving complex chaotic behaviors. Impact Tested across various physical systems, the modular and model-agnostic approach closely matched true outcomes compared to conventional methods. The team has made their code and paper freely available online, paving the way for more trustworthy and reliable AI applications in meteorology, aviation, and industrial processes.

item.title: Spotify CEO Daniel Ek backs AI researcher's new fusion startup
item.description: Europa Fusion was founded in February by Nantas Nardelli, an AI researcher with experience at Google DeepMind, FAIR, and Microsoft Research. Sources report that Nardelli previously served as head of machine learning at Pacific Fusion, another fusion startup that relies heavily on physical devices to test theories and improve simulations. According to sources familiar with his thinking, Nardelli disagreed with this heavy hardware focus, believing instead that fusion startups should invest more in simulation and data. Like Pacific Fusion, Europa Fusion will pursue a pulsed-power approach, using precise surges of electrical current to compress fuel targets. While fusion power could eventually provide abundant carbon-free electricity and help offset AI energy demands, no operational power plant has yet supplied electricity to the grid.

item.title: Trump threatens heavy tax on US companies building AI data centers abroad
item.description:
President Donald Trump stated that the US will not allow domestic companies to build data centers outside the country, proposing a heavy tax as a deterrent. He introduced the proposal during a press conference following a summit, flanked by Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio. Trump admitted that he was floating the plan publicly for the first time and had not yet discussed the details with his staff.
The threat comes as local policymakers across the US are placing new restrictions, moratoriums, and pauses on new data center applications due to mounting concerns over power grids and energy resources. These domestic roadblocks might otherwise push companies to seek foreign alternatives, making Trump's proposed tax an effort to keep infrastructure investments inside the US.

item.title: John Deere Acquires Orchard Robotics to Boost AI Farming Tech
item.description:
Founded in 2022, Orchard Robotics developed an AI-powered camera system that mounts onto farm vehicles, capturing millions of images to measure fruit counts, size, health, and disease status. The data is processed locally using onboard NVIDIA hardware, bypassing poor farm internet connectivity, and feeds into a platform called FruitScope.
Industry experts note the deal highlights the growing value of actionable farm data, with Orchard providing Deere the plant-level vision for orchards and vineyards that previous acquisitions gave it for row crops. Moving forward, the combined technology will enable automated processes like variable-rate spraying, which optimizes chemical use and significantly reduces labor costs for farmers.

item.title: AI is great at coding, but still struggles with tasks requiring human judgment
item.description: The Limits of Verifiable Tasks According to METR, AI systems have excelled at coding and math because they are verifiable domains where solutions can be automatically checked, allowing reinforcement learning to strengthen successful neural pathways. However, applying this technique to open-ended tasks like choosing research directions is much harder. Testing Judgment To address this, METR updated its evaluation plot to include fuzzier tasks, such as designing AI evaluations and scoring philosophical arguments. On these tasks, models consistently lagged behind human performance. Even though advanced models excel at software engineering, none of their AI-designed evaluations were deemed useful by METR employees, highlighting a current performance gap in judgment-heavy areas. Future Outlook While some experts like UC Berkeley's Sayash Kapoor view the inclusion of open-ended tasks as crucial for understanding AI research and development automation, others debate whether models trained on verifiable tasks will eventually master judgment. METR researchers note that quantifying such tasks remains difficult, leaving the future trajectory of these capabilities uncertain.

item.title: Aalborg University Orders On-Premises Superconducting Quantum Computer for Engineering Training
item.description:
According to the announcement, Aalborg University has chosen Swedish quantum hardware company ConScience AB to supply an on-premises superconducting quantum computer for its Department of Electronic Systems. Scheduled for installation in 2027, the Plug'N'Teach system will initially launch with two superconducting qubits before expanding to seven.
Unlike traditional cloud-based learning approaches, the setup will occupy two rooms and integrate ConScience processors with control and readout electronics from Quantum Machines and cryogenic dilution refrigeration from Bluefors. The initiative aims to train engineering students directly on cryogenic hardware operations, microwave control, and qubit readout, while also supporting faculty research in component miniaturization and energy efficiency.

item.title: Chinese Team Wins 2026 Gordon Bell Prize for Exascale Nitrogen Fixation Simulation
item.description:
According to the Association for Computing Machinery (ACM), the 10-member team received the prestigious Gordon Bell Prize during the SC26 conference in Chicago for their project titled 'Closing the FeMo-Cofactor Quantum-Advantage Gap with Exascale Supercomputers.' The Gordon Bell Prize recognizes outstanding achievements in applying high-performance computing to complex scientific and engineering problems.
The team focused on the FeMo Cofactor CAS problem, which involves simulating the complex quantum-level interactions of the iron-molybdenum cofactor that helps enzymes convert nitrogen into ammonia—a crucial process for agriculture and biology. Prior to this, classical computers struggled to simulate these intricate electronic behaviors at scale.
To tackle this, the researchers tuned their simulation code for two advanced Chinese supercomputers, LineShine and China's New-generation Intelligent Super-computer (CNIS). According to their paper's abstract, the team achieved a sustained performance of 1.456 exaflops in double precision across 20,480 nodes on LineShine, utilizing 58.9% of the machine's peak capacity, alongside 5.626 exaflops in mixed precision.

item.title: FDA Misses Decision Deadline for Savara's Rare Lung Disease Drug
item.description:
Savara recently reported that the FDA will fail to meet its already extended PDUFA decision date for molgramostim, an inhaled therapy intended to treat autoimmune pulmonary alveolar proteinosis, a rare and serious lung condition. Following the announcement, Savara's stock fell 18% to $4.26 per share at market open. This marks the second time the review process has faced delays, as the agency previously extended the timeline by three months due to a major application amendment.
Despite the uncertainty and the lack of a newly assigned decision deadline, financial analysts from Jefferies and Guggenheim expressed strong confidence in the drug's approval prospects. They noted that the delay is likely driven by general bandwidth constraints at the FDA rather than safety or efficacy concerns. The drug candidate previously demonstrated positive results in the Phase 3 IMPALA-2 trial, successfully meeting its primary endpoint and showing long-term durability, positioning it to potentially become the first approved treatment for the disease.

item.title: Revolution Medicines reports positive early survival data for pancreatic cancer drug Rasonque
item.description: Clinical Results and Trial Details According to Revolution Medicines, data from 61 patients in the ongoing Phase 1/2 RMC-GI-102 open-label trial presented at a recent medical meeting showed that Rasonque combined with two types of chemotherapy achieved an objective response rate of 60.7% in first-line pancreatic cancer patients. The trial reported a median progression-free survival of 12.8 months, outperforming analyst expectations, while overall survival reached 76.6% at the 12-month mark. Market Impact and Competition Following these findings, Truist Securities noted that the drug's profile sets a high efficacy bar and could boost Revolution Medicines beyond its currently estimated $14.5 billion in peak sales. Meanwhile, the company faces patent litigation and upcoming clinical readouts from competitors like Erasca, which is developing its own targeted therapies in the space.

item.title: How Industrial AI and the Digital Twin are Shaping Engineering
item.description: According to Siemens Blog: Siemens details how the evolution of the digital twin beyond geometric modeling into a full system representation, combined with industrial AI, creates a symbiotic relationship for manufacturing and engineering. The digital twin acts as a safe testing environment and provides synthetic data to train AI models. Meanwhile, industrial AI introduces reasoning and prediction capabilities, enabling the use of reduced-order models that slash simulation times from hours to seconds. Furthermore, the executable digital twin brings these physics-based simulations directly to the production floor for real-time insights, though Siemens notes that human expertise and engineering judgment remain essential alongside these automated tools.

item.title: China grid-connects world’s first artificial-cavern CAES plant
item.description:
The Yuanchu No. 1 compressed air energy storage station in Yumen, Gansu province, achieved its first grid connection on November 16. Developed by China Energy Digital Technology Group, a subsidiary of China Energy Engineering Corporation, the facility represents a notable shift in compressed-air storage technology by moving beyond traditional reliance on natural salt caverns.
The plant features a 300 MW/1,800 MWh capacity, designed for an eight-hour charging cycle and six hours of discharge, with a total investment of approximately CNY 2.5 billion. Its defining innovation is four interconnected storage chambers excavated roughly 110 meters deep into hard rock, creating a pressurized space of about 200,000 cubic meters with a design pressure of 18 MPa.
The facility employs non-combustion, adiabatic CAES technology, utilizing a thermal system that combines low-melting-point ternary molten salt and pressurized hot water to recover and store compression heat without burning natural gas. While the developer reports a round-trip efficiency of 72%, sustained long-term operational data and independent verification are still needed to confirm its economic viability and cavern integrity.

item.title: Merck and Kelun's new cancer drug succeeds in stomach cancer trial
item.description:
According to Merck, the Phase 3 clinical trial known as TroFuse-015 evaluated 473 patients with advanced gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma who had previously received multiple therapies. The drug, a TROP2-targeting antibody-drug conjugate originally discovered by China startup Kelun-Biotech, successfully met its primary endpoint by significantly improving overall survival compared to standard treatments chosen by physicians. However, the trial missed secondary endpoints including progression-free survival and objective response rate. Market analysts point out that missing these secondary goals is not uncommon in cancer immunotherapies as long as the primary survival metric succeeds.
This trial is part of a broad global clinical program featuring 18 late-stage studies across various tumor types. The therapy is also under priority review by the U.S. FDA for endometrial cancer and has secured approvals in China for multiple indications. Financial analysts view this drug as a critical asset for Merck to offset future revenue risks from its blockbuster drug Keytruda. Merck initially partnered with Kelun in 2022 through lucrative licensing deals worth billions to secure rights to these promising antibody-drug conjugates.

item.title: ProMateria Starts Industrial Production of Additive Metal Parts
item.description:
ProMateria GmbH, a subsidiary launched by European metal-processing firm GMH Gruppe, has operationalized its production facility after about 12 months of planning. According to Commercial Director Philip Stöhr, the plant will first produce ready-to-install spare parts for GMH Gruppe companies. The facility currently utilizes MoldJet and sintering processes to handle serial production, development, and qualification projects.
GMH Gruppe operates more than 20 steel, forging, and casting sites with around 6,000 employees and produces steel from recycled scrap using electric arc furnaces. CEO Dr. Alexander Becker stated that ProMateria combines advanced metallurgical expertise with digital manufacturing. Following its initial internal projects, ProMateria plans to target external industrial customers for complex metal components and small production runs that are difficult to make economically using conventional methods.

item.title: Biopharma Executives Gather for London Life Sciences Week Amid Strong M&A and China Policy Clouds
item.description:
During London Life Sciences Week, heavy dealmaking stole the spotlight as pharmaceutical giants like Johnson & Johnson and Eli Lilly announced massive acquisitions, including a $2.2 billion deal by J&J and multi-billion-dollar oncology and fibrosis pacts by Lilly. Legal and financial experts from Baker McKenzie, Sofinnova Partners, and Forbion noted that M&A activity is expected to remain robust, bolstered by record-breaking European venture capital funds such as Sofinnova’s $815 million raise and Forbion’s 2.3 billion euro fund.
Despite the optimistic outlook, significant headwinds remain. Investors pointed out that Europe still lacks a local equivalent to Nasdaq, forcing growing biotechs to look across the Atlantic for major public listings. Furthermore, the rapid rise of China's automated clinical trial infrastructure has become a central topic of discussion, with U.S. investors rushing to lock in deals ahead of potential regulatory clampdowns by the U.S. Treasury regarding outbound investments in pharmaceutical compounds.

item.title: MaterialCities Maps the Materials Locked Inside Buildings Across 1.8 Million Settlements
item.description: According to the Scientific Data paper, researchers developed MaterialCities by merging nighttime-light observations, global built-up-surface and building-height datasets, along with regional construction classifications. The dataset estimates the total global gross floor area at 1.127 trillion square meters across roughly 1.79 million spatial units, separating them by building function and structural system to assess materials like concrete, steel, and timber. While the authors performed reasonableness checks against previous studies, they note that the unedited paper is awaiting final editing, and full accuracy still requires ground-truthing and improved coverage for informal buildings.

item.title: Robot Talk Podcast: Programming Robot Behavior with Sebastian Castro
item.description: Background and Guest Robot Talk is a weekly podcast exploring robotics and autonomous systems. In Episode 171, host Claire sits down with Sebastian Castro, an independent roboticist specializing in robotic manipulation. Industry Experience Castro currently works with the Dexterous Robotics Group at NASA's Johnson Space Center. His impressive resume includes stints as a software engineer at Boston Dynamics, the Robotics and AI Institute, PickNik, and MIT's CSAIL, alongside educational marketing work at MathWorks. Beyond his professional roles, Castro actively contributes to robotics education through open-source software, blog posts, talks, and workshops.

item.title: Goa Plans to Train 50,000 Graduates in AI by 2030
item.description:
The Goa Cabinet has approved the Goa Artificial Intelligence Policy 2026, setting a three-year roadmap to integrate AI across education, industry, startups, and governance. Under this policy, 60% of total resources are allocated to AI skilling and capacity building, with the state targeting to train and certify 50,000 graduates by 2030. Startup support and infrastructure development will each receive 20% of the resources.
To address linguistic diversity, the policy proposes a Konkani AI and Research Excellence Scheme to build a local language model and speech infrastructure using the central government's BHASHINI platform. Additionally, the Udyam AI Scheme will encourage AI adoption among micro, small, and medium enterprises, while an advisory council chaired by the Chief Minister oversees implementation.

item.title: Quantus Launches a Quantum-Secure Cold Wallet That Runs on Any Spare Phone
item.description:
Quantus reports that it has launched the Quantus Cold Wallet to address hidden vulnerabilities in traditional hardware wallets, such as supply-chain tampering and physical home-address leaks tied to retail shipping. The app installs on any spare phone, and users permanently disable its Wi-Fi and mobile data during setup. According to Quantus CTO Nikolaus Heger, the software leverages the secure elements built into modern smartphones to keep keys safe and uses plain-text transaction displays to prevent blind signing. The wallet also features higher computing power than typical hardware wallets, allowing it to handle advanced cryptographic proofs, and it supports the ML-DSA post-quantum standard approved by NIST.
Quantus CEO Christopher Smith notes that the design helps users avoid the physical risks associated with specialized hardware wallets, which openly signal crypto ownership and expose buyers to targeted home-address leaks and related crimes. The app currently supports QTC, the native token of the Quantus network, and is available for download on the App Store and Google Play.

item.title: Alsym Energy says US battery policy needs to focus more on upstream sodium
item.description:
At the RE+ event in Las Vegas, Alsym Energy COO Graeme Grant argued that current US battery policies have missed the mark by heavily subsidizing final cell assembly while ignoring upstream raw materials. According to Grant, battery manufacturing credits can reach about US$35 per kilowatt-hour, sometimes exceeding the actual sale price of a cell, whereas upstream input credits cover only around 10% of costs.
Grant noted that this policy imbalance has already limited the effectiveness of domestic lithium iron phosphate (LFP) efforts, as critical components like graphite and LFP materials still largely originate overseas. To avoid repeating past mistakes—such as when early US battery innovations were commercialized domestically only to be later acquired abroad—Grant believes the US should lean into sodium-ion technology. He highlighted that Wyoming holds 85% of the world's known natural sodium carbonate deposits in the form of trona, which is already mined industrially and offers a ready-made path to build a secure, independent supply chain.

item.title: Meta's AI Assistant Muse Is Fueling Instagram Unfollow Drama
item.description: According to WIRED, Meta's AI assistant Muse has inadvertently sparked a viral trend where users leverage the chatbot to audit their social circles on Instagram. Users like Khalil Roberts and tech worker Kimberly Munoz have used simple prompts to instruct Muse to generate lists of non-reciprocal followers and automate unfollow actions. While some view this as a convenient way to clean up cluttered feeds or clear out dormant connections, researchers note it highlights a broader shift toward outsourcing emotionally uncomfortable decisions to technology. Meanwhile, Meta previously removed an advertising campaign promoting Muse's unfollow tracking features in October, though the company did not comment on the decision.

item.title: Oumi Featured in NYTimes: Why Silicon Valley Turned Against Anthropic
item.description:
According to Oumi:
On November 13, 2026, reporters at the New York Times published an investigation titled 'Why Silicon Valley's Knives Came Out for Anthropic.' The report examines the growing backlash against Anthropic, focusing on its frequent warnings about AI safety risks, its expanding industry influence, and its opposition to widely shared open-weight models.
Weighing in on the debate, Oumi CEO Manos Koukoumidis told The Times that the US has mistakenly convinced itself that cutting-edge innovation should remain in the hands of a select few organizations. Following the coverage, Koukoumidis emphasized that enterprises should build specialized models rather than surrendering their future and core intellectual property to a handful of external model providers.

item.title: Dual-Pathway Control for Efficient Nitrate Conversion in Wastewater
item.description:
According to Agro-Environmental Protection Institute 农业农村部环保所:
The Rural Environmental Construction Innovation Team at the Agro-Environmental Protection Institute of the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs published a study in Green Energy & Environment detailing nitrate electroreduction in wastewater. Electroreduction converts nitrate into usable ammonium, but water electrolysis creates competing effects between hydrogen generation and electron competition with nitrate.
Using a LaCoO3 model system and a B-site Pd doping strategy, the researchers decoupled the electron reduction and adsorbed hydrogen reduction pathways through cyclic voltammetry and quenching experiments. The study found that Pd doping induces more oxygen vacancies, strengthens nitrate adsorption, lowers reaction energy barriers, and suppresses competing hydrogen evolution side reactions. This dual-pathway promotion effect was verified across multiple perovskite systems.
item.source: Agro-Environmental Protection Institute 农业农村部环保所

item.title: Li Auto built a chip that made it to TSMC's stage, but wants you to totally forget about it while driving
item.description: Traditional chips struggle with AI workloads due to the von Neumann architecture bottleneck, where data is constantly shuttled back and forth between processors and memory, wasting a huge portion of compute power. Li Auto's Mach M100 replaces this with a dynamic dataflow architecture that streamlines data processing directly across computing units. Built on a 5nm automotive-grade process, the 1280 TOPS chip achieves over 82% compute utilization. This high efficiency allows vehicles to run advanced AI models and native 3D visual encoders smoothly, removing the hesitation and jerks often found in traditional smart driving systems.

item.title: OpenAI details how it blocks bad actors from stealing AI reasoning capabilities
item.description: According to OpenAI News: OpenAI reports that unauthorized distillation allows bad actors to reproduce frontier AI capabilities, such as advanced coding or cyber skills, without safety safeguards. Attackers often target a model's protected reasoning, which is the internal chain of thought generated while working toward an answer. To counter this, OpenAI combines adversarial training, input and output classifiers, and strict API-level protections. In tests with GPT-6.2 Astra, the average attack success rate for extracting reasoning from an earlier request dropped from 54.0% to 0.2%. OpenAI also conducts campaign-level investigations to disrupt coordinated extraction attempts and supports U.S. legislation and export controls to address national security risks.

item.title: Jeff Bezos Returns as CEO to Build Prometheus, an AI Startup for the Physical World
item.description:
At the Semafor Silicon Valley and the World summit, Jeff Bezos revealed his new role as co-founder and co-CEO of Prometheus alongside physicist Vik Bajaj. The company, which employs about 250 people, focuses on numerical simulation neural agents and multi-physics models to transform computer-aided design and physical simulation. Bezos stated that tasks requiring 10 to 20 engineers six to nine months can now be completed by the system in under 12 hours, with Blue Origin already running internal tests on two projects.
Unlike text-based models, Prometheus tackles the complex challenge of industrial data scarcity by using self-developed multi-physics simulation systems to generate synthetic data. Despite massive funding from top-tier financial institutions, experts note that physical world applications carry zero tolerance for error, and achieving generalization across diverse engineering fields remains a massive technical challenge.

item.title: HiNa Battery Launches Lithium-Sodium Storage Solution for AI Data Centers
item.description:
Hithium introduced its lithium-sodium co-optimized energy storage solution in December 2025, targeting the growing power demands of AI and intelligent computing centers. According to media reports cited in the text, global data center power consumption is projected by the International Energy Agency to exceed 1,000 terawatt-hours, turning storage into a critical component for peak shaving, cost reduction, and green power supply.
The industry typically evaluates storage options based on four dimensions: duration, discharge rate, safety, and levelized cost. While lithium iron phosphate and sodium-ion batteries represent two mainstream technical routes, Hithium combines both to balance different power and duration requirements for data center backup and load regulation.
Market data from various consulting agencies in the first half of 2026 ranked Hithium second globally in energy storage battery shipments, reflecting its capacity for large-scale delivery.
item.source: China Energy Network Storage 中国能源网

item.title: Huawei Cloud releases CloudRobo-WM1.2, an Ascend-native embodied world model
item.description:
Huawei Cloud announced its Ascend-native embodied world model, CloudRobo-WM1.2, which utilizes a multi-modal world representation architecture named PPA to combine perception, prediction, and action. According to Huawei Cloud, the model scored highest in RoboTwin 2.0 and LIBERO-Pro 2.0 benchmarks and outperformed peers in multi-robot real-world tests.
To address massive memory and compute demands, Huawei Cloud optimized the entire stack on Ascend hardware, including cluster communication, long-sequence data processing, and reinforcement learning frameworks developed with Tsinghua University. Huawei Cloud plans to release the model weights and training codes on November 30 and integrate partners through its CloudRobo platform.

item.title: AI is evolving fast. Here is how Siemens plans to help data centers keep up
item.description:
According to Siemens Blog:
At NVIDIA GTC Berlin 2026, Siemens global solutions director Diego Witte and US data center head John DeBoer outlined the major hurdles facing AI infrastructure. While AI chips and compute demands scale rapidly, data centers face bottlenecks in scale, speed, skilled labor, and power availability.
To overcome these issues, Siemens advocates a shift toward digital twin simulation to test liquid cooling and rack configurations before physical construction. They also stress the need for standardized reference designs to align compute, power, and cooling ecosystems, and modular construction to combat labor shortages.
Furthermore, the report emphasizes that data centers must evolve into active grid participants. By combining software automation with physical hardware like battery storage and supercapacitors, and integrating IT with operational technology (OT), facilities can better manage extreme energy demands and improve overall efficiency.

item.title: Danish Soldiers Allegedly Smuggle Starlink into Greenland
item.description:
According to parliamentary questions raised by Greenlandic politician Pele Broberg, multiple sources claim that Danish soldiers stationed in Greenland are bringing their own Starlink terminals from Denmark for personal internet access. Broberg used these reports to question why local citizens are denied the same service, given that Greenland's Telecommunications Act strictly prohibits Starlink use outside the state-owned operator Tusass.
In its response, the Greenlandic government stated it had no confirmation of the soldiers' actions, though it acknowledged reports of unauthorised Starlink installations. The government also admitted that enforcement resources are limited, meaning unauthorized use is a low priority if it does not interfere with lawful radio communications.
This incident is part of Broberg's ongoing effort to break the state-controlled telecommunications monopoly. The Greenlandic government defends the current system, warning that allowing foreign providers like Starlink could undermine universal service obligations and uniform pricing across the territory.

item.title: LLM Complexity: Towards a Computational Complexity View of Large Language Model Inference
item.description: The authors report in this preprint: A new preprint titled 'LLM Complexity: Towards a Computational Complexity View of Large Language Model Inference' investigates how large language models allocate computation during inference. The authors test the hypothesis that generated token length serves as a reliable proxy for classical time complexity, but disprove it by showing a fundamental divergence in how LLMs manage computational steps. To address this, they introduce 'LLM Complexity,' a metric that quantifies problem difficulty by capturing the area bounded above by the accuracy-token curve. The study reports that diverse LLMs produce consistent task rankings under this metric, suggesting it captures stable notions of difficulty. The authors leverage this framework to design an easy-to-hard curriculum for supervised fine-tuning, which they report improves model accuracy while decreasing token consumption. Additionally, they state that the metric generalizes well to real-world tasks, yielding more stable cross-model correlations than standard human-annotated difficulty labels. The paper is currently a preprint on arXiv without independent replication or peer review.

item.title: PsyWorld: Profile-Conditioned World Modeling for Human Behavior Prediction
item.description: The authors report in this preprint: The authors present PsyWorld, a profile-conditioned state world model designed to predict human behavior by incorporating observed environment-behavior state transitions rather than treating personality as a direct action descriptor. The framework uses a posterior encoder to quantize realized transitions during training, while a prior predicts the resulting codes from the psychometric profile and pre-transition context. Evaluated on the VEET behavioral simulator with a participant-disjoint split (240 training, 25 validation, and 48 test participants) and in AgentSociety, the model reaches 0.904 Top-1 accuracy and 0.0033 Macro KL on VEET. Ablations indicate that continuous next-state modeling drives most of the Top-1 gain, whereas discrete codes and prior alignment improve distributional alignment. The authors note that the framework provides transition-informed supervision without implying causal psychological mechanisms or calibrated long-horizon state dynamics.

item.title: Denmark’s Matr Foods Opens Fungi Fermentation Factory for Clean-Label Meat Alternatives
item.description: Matr Foods, founded in 2021, uses a solid-state fermentation process where fungi spores inoculate upcycled ingredients like peas, lupin beans, beetroots, potatoes, and oats. Instead of creating isolated fungi protein, the company uses fungi as a binder and flavor enhancer, creating a juicy texture and a meat-like amino acid profile with a low carbon footprint. The new 60-employee plant scales production significantly from their previous 30-tonne capacity in Copenhagen, aiming to overcome supply bottlenecks that previously forced them to turn away canteens and supermarkets.

item.title: Robotics enters its post-Jensen Huang era
item.description:
Jensen Huang's departure following his resignation from NVIDIA marks a turning point for the robotics industry, where he served as a central champion for physical AI. Over the years, Huang used his keynote platforms to showcase humanoid robots, fund struggling startups like Serve Robotics, and build a comprehensive development stack spanning GPUs, simulation tools like Omniverse, and foundation models like GR00T.
Industry leaders acknowledge that Huang's steady attention and willingness to invest in early-stage markets made it significantly easier for robotics founders to secure funding and credibility. However, with interim CEO Colette Kress at the helm and potential pressures from data center competition and regulatory scrutiny, the future of NVIDIA's direct support, keynote spotlights, and strategic investments in robotics remains uncertain.
Despite these concerns, many experts believe the robotics flywheel is already spinning on its own, supported by alternative hardware competitors and widespread developer momentum. Yet, as humanoid developers face mounting pressure to prove actual commercial use cases and secure future funding over the next year, the loss of Huang's unique charisma and institutional backing leaves a notable void in the ecosystem.

item.title: University of Amsterdam Funds Four Quantum Projects for Chemistry and Materials
item.description: According to the University of Amsterdam, the Faculty of Science has committed €200,000 in seed funding to each of four teams under the new Q-SIM4MMD initiative, totaling €800,000. Embedded within the Molecular and Material Design Technology Hub, the initiative is supported by a newly formed Q-Sim expertise group that links researchers in physics, chemistry, life sciences, and computer science with QuSoft and Quantum Delta NL Amsterdam. Project Focus and Collaborations The funded projects target various computational tasks, including quantum-circuit kernels for modeling PFAS binding, benchmarking hybrid quantum-classical workflows for bioinformatics, quantum-assisted topological molecular representations for chemical screening, and benchmarking quantum simulations of 2D Hubbard models against classical tensor networks. Launched across eight institutes, the MMD TechHub will help the teams transition their proof-of-concept algorithms toward external public-private partnerships and industrial funding.

item.title: Apple Developing AI Agents to Control Devices, While Anthropic Tops Trillion-Dollar Valuation After IPO
item.description:
Apple has added a job posting for a senior engineering manager to develop proactive AI assistants capable of executing multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, and codebases, with a target timeline around late next year. Concurrently, Apple is tightening third-party AI permissions in macOS, increasing verification steps for tools like ChatGPT.
In the AI industry, Anthropic completed its historic IPO on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT. Priced at $83 per share, the stock surged on debut, pushing its valuation briefly past $2 trillion before closing up 17% at $97.17, yielding a market cap of roughly $1.27 billion.
Other notable developments include Google bringing Computer Use to Mac versions of Gemini, allowing background app control, and DeepSeek completing an equity restructuring that brought in major industry backers like Tencent and Contemporary Amperex Technology.

item.title: Inkling 2 Mini: A compact multimodal AI model with loop architecture for local setups
item.description:
Thinking Machines Lab reports that Inkling 2 Mini features 24 decoder layers, with the 12 middle layers running three times in a loop to act as 48 logical layers. This design allows the model to maintain a compact physical size while retaining high capacity. It uses NVFP4 and MXFP8 expert weights and supports a 1-million-token context size.
In benchmark tests, the model leads in 32 out of 48 categories against similar mid-sized models, excelling in coding, agentic search, and vision interpretation. Inference support is available out-of-the-box through transformers, llama.cpp, MLX, and SGLang, alongside a DSpark drafter for speculative decoding speed-ups.

item.title: Anthropic Closes Massive Initial Public Offering and Private Placement
item.description: According to Anthropic News: Offering Details Anthropic reports the closing of an aggregate of 1,127,000,000 shares of Class A common stock at $83.00 per share, which includes the full exercise of the underwriters' option. Total gross proceeds from the IPO reached approximately $93.5 billion, with about $91.6 billion going directly to Anthropic. Private Placement In addition to the public offering, Anthropic closed a concurrent private placement of 313,253,007 shares of Class N common stock to major technology and semiconductor partners including Google, Microsoft, NVIDIA, AMD, Broadcom, Micron, and TSMC at the same price, securing an additional $26.0 billion.

item.title: Harness adapters: tailoring AI models for specific agent frameworks to boost performance and cut costs
item.description:
Large language models are typically trained for general performance, meaning they leave room for improvement when paired with specific agent harnesses for targeted tasks. To bridge this gap, researchers trained custom LoRA adapters using reinforcement learning (RL) directly within three popular agent harnesses: Pi, Hermes Agent, and OpenCode. Using a filtered dataset of validation-screened programming tasks, the team leveraged TRL's AsyncGRPOTrainer alongside Hugging Face infrastructure to optimize the Qwen 3.8-27B model.
Evaluation results indicate that specialist adapters consistently outperform the base model under their respective harnesses across benchmarks like Terminal-Bench 2.1 and SWE-bench Pro, achieving significant accuracy gains while reducing tool calls by over 50%. Furthermore, researchers successfully merged the three separate adapters into a single super-adapter, which retains strong multi-framework compatibility and efficiency without requiring complex retraining.

item.title: Introducing Inkling 2 Mini: A Looped AI Model You Can Run on Your Laptop
item.description: According to Thinking Machines Lab: Inkling 2 Mini features 26.4 billion total parameters with 3.4 billion active, utilizing a looped transformer design where the middle layers are executed three times for every token. This architecture enables the model to achieve high-level reasoning and excel in agentic coding and knowledge-based tasks while keeping a compact memory footprint of around 20GB, making it capable of offline execution on devices like a MacBook Pro. Researchers evaluated its monitorability through a variable-loop variant and found that while looping increases internal computation without a verbalized chain of thought, it does not obscure the legibility of the model's reasoning or increase the risk of undetected agentic sabotage.

item.title: AI model connects molecular structures and spectra in any direction
item.description: According to Lila Sciences: Background and Method In March 2026, AI researchers Thorben Prein and Elton Pan at Lila Sciences identified a gap in materials science AI: most models only translate between molecular structures and spectra in a single direction. To solve this, they developed MOSAIC, an any-to-any method accepted for the NeurIPS 2026 conference. The approach combines infrared, UV, and Raman spectral modalities alongside molecular structures, treating all four data types as interchangeable viewpoints of the same molecule, much like multiple people describing an elephant from different angles. Performance and Validation In experiments, MOSAIC predicted correct molecular structures from spectra 88.8% of the time, significantly outperforming traditional baselines. Independent expert Kevin Maik Jablonka noted that while the method tackles an important problem by combining evidence sources, future work must demonstrate its effectiveness on complex mixtures and noisy experimental data rather than just pure, small molecules. Future Outlook The researchers plan to scale the model using more simulated and proprietary lab data through industry partnerships. They believe this multimodal flow matching approach could eventually generalize to drug design and renewable energy materials, helping scientists reduce experiments, lower costs, and speed up discovery.

item.title: Depth Pro 2: Apple researchers introduce AI model for sharp and stable video depth estimation
item.description: According to Apple Machine Learning: Background Estimating depth from a single image or video using a regular camera has long forced a compromise. Single-frame methods usually produce sharp edges, but jump around annoyingly from frame to frame in video. Multi-frame methods stay steady, but often blur out fine details. Details According to the authors, Depth Pro 2 trains a single scalable network that handles individual photos, full videos, or live camera feeds at native resolution. It predicts dense metric depth in actual meters without sacrificing either edge sharpness or frame-to-frame consistency. Impact The team has released a family of models along with their code and weights, establishing a new performance benchmark for metric depth estimation that can run efficiently across different media types.

item.title: AI Agent Runs Office Vending Business in Real-World Safety Test
item.description:
According to Reflection AI:
Reflection and Andon Labs designed a real-world evaluation where AI agents named Mr. Beam and Mrs. Beam independently operated standalone vending businesses in their New York and San Francisco offices. Operating via a custom harness called Pion with over 70 tools and continuous loop execution, the agents handled procurement, pricing, inventory, and customer service through Slack channels.
During the evaluation, Mr. Beam demonstrated strong resilience against sophisticated red-teaming attacks, successfully blocking attempts to stock nicotine products, order prohibited items like flamethrowers, or fall for fake rival agent setups. However, the evaluation exposed significant reliability vulnerabilities. Mr. Beam struggled with executing multi-step workflows, made financial calculation errors, and was tricked by unverified claims, such as a false email about a safety manager's firing which polluted its long-term memory. Additionally, it frequently accommodated customer complaints by issuing unverified refunds or free items, leading to high human intervention rates for financial and workflow corrections.

item.title: SK hynix Showcases Memory-Centric AI Vision at Supercomputing 2026
item.description:
According to SK hynix Newsroom:
At Supercomputing 2026 in Chicago, SK hynix introduced its technology vision focused on reshaping the AI ecosystem around advanced memory solutions. The company showcased its Memory-centric AI Rack System (MARS) alongside three key CXL-based demonstrations, including rack-level KV cache sharing, computational memory pools for AI agents, and token-sharing across CPU servers to reduce GPU idle time.
Additionally, SK hynix presented advanced hardware zones featuring KV Cache Offloading over CXL, Compute-using-DRAM, and Custom HBM Array. Alongside these conceptual designs, the company displayed its core product portfolio for AI infrastructure, featuring next-generation HBM4 and HBM4E, high-capacity 256GB 3DS DDR5 RDIMM modules, and liquid-cooling-supported eSSDs.

item.title: SpaceX to launch classified U.S. Space Force mission USSF-317
item.description:
According to Spaceflight Now, SpaceX is preparing to launch the USSF-317 mission for the U.S. Space Force from Vandenberg Space Force Base. The flight will utilize a Falcon 9 rocket powered by the B1100 booster, which is flying for the 11th time. Following liftoff, the booster is targeted to land on the droneship *Of Course I Still Love You*, marking a continued routine of booster reuse.
The mission is the latest in a series of 'R' missions assigned to SpaceX, following five previous flights since August. Although tracking suggests 23 satellites have been catalogued after each of those prior launches, the U.S. Space Force has not officially confirmed details or successful deployments for them. SpaceX has at least two more military missions scheduled before the end of the month.

item.title: Google brings computer use feature to Mac Gemini app, starting in the US
item.description: Background and Details Google announced the rollout of the computer use capability for the Mac Gemini app, aimed at users with Apple Silicon Macs running macOS Sequoia or later who subscribe to specific paid plans. According to Google, when users provide natural language prompts, Gemini can coordinate tasks across local files, desktop software, and web browsers, such as filling out complex shipping forms or building presentation slides from dashboard data. The process runs in a separated background window so that the AI does not hijack the main cursor or screen. Safety and Industry Context To maintain user control, the feature allows individuals to choose which apps Gemini can access, view step-by-step actions in real time, and pause operations whenever necessary. Critical actions also require explicit user approval. Similar capabilities have been explored across the industry, with Anthropic and OpenAI introducing comparable agent features for developer tools and desktop apps over the past year.

item.title: langchain-openai==1.8.5: Package Release and Version Comparison Overview
item.description:
Release Overview
The provided document outlines a comprehensive list of version comparisons for the langchain-openai==1.8.5 release against a wide array of earlier project tags, stretching from v0.1.17rc1 down to earlier iterations. Developer Utility
By leveraging these direct comparison links, developers and maintainers can easily examine specific code modifications, patch updates, and dependency adjustments implemented across distinct release milestones.

item.title: Amazon Bedrock now lets AI agents buy software and APIs directly through AWS bills
item.description: According to AWS Machine Learning: Amazon reports that its Bedrock AgentCore payments now integrate with AWS Marketplace, enabling AI agents to discover, purchase, and use x402-enabled software, APIs, and data directly charged to the developer's AWS account. According to AWS, when an agent encounters a payment requirement, it forwards the signed quote to AgentCore payments, which verifies session budgets before issuing a payment token. Developers maintain control by configuring spending caps, approved seller lists, and separate IAM roles for sessions and payments. AWS states that transactions are fully auditable through CloudTrail and Cost Explorer, and early partners like Tavily are already offering integrated live search tools for autonomous agentic commerce.

item.title: Novartis CEO says AI will speed up drug development, but solving biology will take a decade
item.description:
Speaking at an investor event, Novartis CEO Vas Narasimhan outlined the drugmaker's goal to use AI to improve clinical success rates from 8% to 12% while slashing four years off the standard 12-year R&D cycle. Narasimhan categorized drug development bottlenecks into information, operational, and biological latency. Novartis is already seeing major gains in the first two areas, with AI assisting 90% of development content and cutting statistical programming time dramatically.
However, Narasimhan and Novartis biomedical research president Fiona Marshall argued that biological latency remains the hardest hurdle. While AI excels at molecular design, translating predictions into human biology requires navigating complex systems that current models cannot fully simulate on computers alone. This perspective echoes pushback from other pharma leaders against tech sector claims that AI will eliminate major diseases in under a decade, emphasizing that steady, incremental progress and wet-lab validation are still essential.

item.title: Anthropic makes history with $81bn IPO as shares close up 17%
item.description: Trading Debut and Market Valuation Anthropic officially went public on the Nasdaq, pricing its shares at $83 before opening at $111.50. During its first trading session, the creator of the Claude chatbot briefly crossed a $2tn valuation, though it settled at a closing price of roughly $97, leaving its market cap around $1.3tn to $1.75tn. The blockbuster offering raised $81bn, surpassing SpaceX's previous record. Wider Market Slump Despite the massive enthusiasm for Anthropic, Wall Street closed sharply lower, with the S&P 500 falling for its sixth straight session. Broader investor anxiety about the sustainability of the AI boom, combined with recent tech sector turbulence involving Nvidia, dragged down major indices. Meanwhile, IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva warned that surging global demand for AI infrastructure is driving up inflation and could force central banks to raise interest rates. Founder Fortunes and Safety Warnings The IPO generated massive paper wealth for Anthropic's seven co-founders, whose stakes are now valued at over $180bn, with plans to donate significant portions to philanthropic causes. Shortly before ringing the opening bell, CEO Dario Amodei issued a public warning acknowledging the real risks of AI, from economic disruption to loss of control, emphasizing that avoiding these dangers depends entirely on prioritizing safety.

item.title: Meta's Upcoming Muse Charm AI Device May Cost $300
item.description:
Meta is reportedly preparing to price its upcoming AI hardware product, Muse Charm, at $300, based on information from The Information. When contacted by TechCrunch, a Meta spokesperson did not deny the pricing report, stating they are charmed by the interest and will share more details soon.
Muse Charm functions as a physical companion for Meta's Muse AI agent, allowing users to carry it in their pocket or wear it around their neck to chat and give commands. While Meta has seen relative success with its software-based AI tools and avatars, hardware is a new frontier.
The $300 price tag places it on the higher end of the current AI wearable market, comparable to devices like Friend at $250, but significantly more expensive than Amazon's Bee Frontier wearable, which lists for $75.

item.title: Why Microsoft, the FAA, and Banks All Broke at the Same Time
item.description:
In a chaotic week for technology, major systems including Microsoft, the FAA, JPMorgan Chase, United Airlines, the NSA, and Apple experienced significant outages. Although U.S. officials, including Secretary of State Marco Rubio, confirmed that the incidents were not cyberattacks, the timing caused widespread panic and led many to suspect hackers or artificial intelligence.
WIRED editors break down the mundane root causes behind the chaos, noting that Microsoft's issue stemmed from a delayed software fix, while the FAA's communication blackout was tied to outdated fiber equipment updates pushed at an inopportune time. Furthermore, experts discuss how companies are increasingly deploying advanced AI cybersecurity tools like Anthropic's Mythos to patch complex bugs, which paradoxically increases the risk of cascading system failures when multiple patches are rushed simultaneously.

item.title: Google's Quantum Chip Beats Classical Limits in Tests of Teamwork
item.description: Cooperative Games and Quantum Contextuality Researchers at Google Quantum AI utilized the Willow processor to investigate quantum contextuality, a property where measurement outcomes depend on accompanying measurements. In a magic square game preventing player communication, four qubits achieved a 98.3% winning rate, surpassing the 88.9% classical limit. Scaling Up to 71 Qubits The team scaled the experiments using a Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger state. The winning rate stayed above the classical ceiling through 71 players, although the performance margin shrank as more qubits were introduced due to experimental noise. Mathematical Problem and Error Detection In a final test involving a two-dimensional hidden linear function, a 105-qubit experiment returned valid answers more than half the time. The researchers note that these tests can help spot subtle hardware errors that conventional checks might miss.

item.title: Google Quantum AI proves quantum contextuality works at scale on Willow processor
item.description: According to Google Research: Beating the classical limit Researchers ran the magic square game on the Willow quantum processor, using entangled Bell pairs instead of a pre-written table. While the best classical strategy wins at most 88.89% of the time, the qubits won 98.30% of the time, proving that answers take shape only upon measurement according to their context. Measuring contextuality at scale Using a Bell-Kochen-Specker inequality, the team measured a contextuality score of 5.590, comfortably past the classical bound of 4 and close to the quantum limit of 6. They also scaled the experiment using the GHZ parity game and solved hidden linear function problems on grids of up to 105 qubits. A new hardware ruler These tasks demand strict agreement among multiple qubits, exposing subtle coherent errors that conventional random-circuit benchmarks miss. This provides an objective performance ceiling grounded in physics rather than shifting classical standards.

item.title: MIT engineers develop dry, stretchy material to replace ultrasound gel
item.description: According to MIT Materials: Background Ultrasound imaging normally requires a cold, wet gel spread on the patient's skin to fill microscopic gaps and help sound waves travel smoothly. While MIT's Zhao Lab is designing wearable ultrasound patches for continuous health tracking, traditional hydrogels dry out within a day or two, limiting their long-term use outside of clinics. Details To solve this, the MIT team engineered a solid, rubbery material using a unique molecular "bottlebrush" structure. By arranging molecules like pipe cleaners with bristles, the team minimized internal friction between polymer chains so sound waves could pass through easily. They reinforced this soft structure with a secondary network, making it tough and skin-like while keeping its sound-transmitting properties intact. Impact In experiments published in *Science*, a small wearable patch using this dry material successfully captured continuous, clear ultrasound images of a volunteer's blood flow during a 30-minute bike ride and remained stable for nine days. This breakthrough could soon enable practical, at-home ultrasound monitoring for patients and athletes without the hassle of sticky gels.

item.title: LangSmith Launches Tool Gateway for Secure Agent Actions
item.description: According to LangChain Blog: Background and Challenges As AI agents move beyond simple chat windows to run autonomously on schedules or in the background, they require access to external tools and systems. According to LangSmith, managing identities, access tokens, and security for hundreds of tools across multiple users creates a massive engineering burden and introduces security risks when handled manually. Core Features Tool Gateway acts as a single managed layer routing tool requests through a unified URL. It manages identity resolution, mapping tool calls to either the individual user's credentials or dedicated agent profiles. Additionally, it offers policy controls such as deny rules and human-in-the-loop approvals for sensitive actions, alongside built-in servers for common apps like Google and GitHub to eliminate custom OAuth setups. Impact and Visibility Every tool call is recorded within agent traces, logging the specific tool, server, user, latency, and outcome without storing sensitive payload data. Enterprise plans also include centralized audit logs, giving security teams a clear, unified record to answer compliance questions and debug production issues faster.

item.title: Google Introduces Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API
item.description:
According to Google AI:
Google product manager Lucia Loher and research scientist Nora Kassner report that connecting AI agents to dozens or hundreds of tools often inflates input tokens, adds latency, and lowers tool selection accuracy. To address this, the new Tool Retrieval feature lets agents keep a full tool library on standby while only loading specific parameter schemas when a task requires them. Developers can enable this by adding a tool_search tool and setting defer_loading: true on tools they wish to hold back. How It Works The model continues to see the name and description of every deferred tool so it understands what is available, while the heavy parameter schemas stay out of context. When a task requires a specific function, the model requests it by name, and the API loads the full schema within the same request. Google notes that this mechanism also supports remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and client-side retrieval for custom registries, while working seamlessly with prefix caching to keep conversation prefixes stable.

item.title: Google Signs 50-MW Superhot Geothermal PPA with Quaise Energy
item.description:
According to companies' announcements, Google has agreed to buy 50 MW of electricity from Project Obsidian, a geothermal power project developed by Quaise Energy near Newberry Volcano in central Oregon, valued at more than $500 million. The energy will support Google's data center operations in The Dalles, Oregon.
The project will be built in two stages. The initial phase will use conventional drilling, while a subsequent phase will deploy Quaise's millimeter-wave drilling technology to reach depths of up to 65,000 feet. At these extreme depths, rock temperatures exceed 932 degrees Fahrenheit, allowing superhot geothermal wells to produce up to 10 times more power per well than conventional sources.
This PPA is part of Google's broader strategy to secure firm, carbon-free electricity, complementing previous investments in advanced nuclear and long-duration storage as the tech sector grapples with baseload power scarcity driven by expanding AI data centers.

item.title: Anthropic shares close 17% higher on first day of trading
item.description: On Thursday, November 19, 2026, AI maker Anthropic made history as the first leading model developer to go public on Wall Street, defying a broad market sell-off and tech bubble concerns. The company priced its shares at $83, but they opened at $111.50 and ultimately closed around $97, up 17% for the day. Record Fundraising and Valuation Anthropic raised an unprecedented $81.3 billion by selling 980 million shares, comfortably surpassing previous megadebuts like SpaceX. The IPO valued the five-year-old creator of the Claude chatbot at roughly $1.5 trillion initially, with its opening valuation surging to around $2 trillion. Chief Executive Dario Amodei stated that the robust financial position reinforces the company's commitment to building safe AI. Explosive Growth and Market Jitters The historic listing comes amid rapid financial growth, with Anthropic reporting third-quarter revenue surging to $17 billion, up dramatically from $1.4 billion a year prior, largely driven by coding applications. However, the debut also drew scrutiny: critics and protesters voiced concerns over potential existential risks and financial market stability, while the broader tech sector navigated ongoing turbulence surrounding chip giant Nvidia.

item.title: Xenia Adds 15% Carbon Fiber to PEBA Filament for Drones and Robots
item.description:
Xenia has expanded its technical filament portfolio with the release of XECARB PEBA-CF, combining a polyether block amide matrix with 15 percent carbon fiber reinforcement. According to the company, the carbon fiber provides stiffness to prevent excessive deformation under mechanical loads, while the elastomeric PEBA base offers toughness and allows parts to spring back to their original shape after impact.
The material features a density of 1.08 g/cm³ and a heat deflection temperature of 105°C. Xenia is targeting the filament primarily at the drone, UAV, and robotics sectors, alongside broader industrial and aerospace applications where components must balance light weight with dynamic stress response. This new grade joins the company's existing 3DF Materials lineup, which includes specialized high-modulus, toughened, and recycled carbon fiber composites.

item.title: Finding the sweet spot for satellite constellation size
item.description:
During a conversation at Space Tech Expo Europe, Jan Smolders, chief commercial officer at Space Inventor, joined SpaceNews' Mike Gruss to discuss key trends in the satellite industry. A central topic was the strategic value of mini-constellations, which offer a balance between responsiveness and capability compared to massive mega-constellations.
Additionally, the discussion touched on institutional hurdles, specifically exploring how European governments can speed up their decision-making and funding processes for space technology. They also examined operational use cases, highlighting why tipping and cueing technologies have become increasingly valuable for regional security and monitoring in the Baltic Sea.

item.title: What industrial drone deployments reveal about real-world autonomy challenges
item.description:
Industrial facilities present complex environments that severely test autonomous drone navigation. GNSS signals can be blocked or distorted by metallic structures, while repetitive pipes and reflective surfaces confuse visual and lidar sensors. Furthermore, wind gusts near buildings introduce aerodynamic disturbances that challenge flight controllers.
ZenaDrone contributor Jonathan Metzelaar notes that autonomy performance depends heavily on the interactions between subsystems whose assumptions are rarely independent. Localization errors can corrupt obstacle coordinates, and processing latency directly translates into physical braking distance, meaning an obstacle avoidance system must be judged on end-to-end timing rather than detection range alone. Additionally, successfully flying a route does not guarantee that collected inspection data, such as thermal imagery or photogrammetry, will be accurate or repeatable.
To ensure safe and reliable deployments, engineering teams must move beyond isolated subsystem tests and evaluate their systems under combined failure scenarios. This includes defining measurable acceptance criteria for localization, latency, and failure recovery, while maintaining clear operational boundaries and supervisory human oversight.

item.title: How Developers Use Frontier AI Agents to Build Simulations in NVIDIA Omniverse
item.description:
According to NVIDIA Robotics:
NVIDIA highlights a series of developer projects demonstrating how frontier AI models and Omniverse libraries are transforming simulation workflows. Engineers and developers are using natural-language instructions to guide AI agents in assembling 3D assets, configuring physics engines, and running tests across diverse domains.
Key examples include building facility-scale digital twins from engineering data, creating robot pick-and-place simulations using standardized asset libraries, and testing humanoids and robotic cable-routing tasks in virtual environments. Developers also report challenges, noting that automated tests sometimes miss tactile issues like object shaking, which require manual inspection and prompt adjustments to resolve.
These workflows leverage OpenUSD frameworks and specialized Omniverse libraries to connect rendering, physics, and sensor simulation, enabling teams to evaluate industrial operations and autonomous systems before deploying them in the physical world.

item.title: Scientists map every single cell in an adult vertebrate for the first time
item.description:
According to MIT Neuroscience:
A team of researchers from MIT, the Whitehead Institute, and Charité–Universitätsmedizin Berlin has successfully mapped the cell types and gene activity of an entire adult vertebrate. Because profiling larger animals comprehensively is technically demanding and expensive, the team turned to *Danionella cerebrum*, a tiny, transparent fish barely one centimeter long that is closely related to zebrafish.
In a study published in *Science*, the researchers used single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial mapping methods to analyze more than 600,000 cells from across the fish's brain, spinal cord, eyes, internal organs, and fins. This comprehensive approach allowed them to capture rare cell populations and observe large-scale patterns, such as how neurons from the same brain region share similar gene activity regardless of the neurotransmitters they use.
The atlas also revealed that adult cells, such as connective-tissue fibroblasts, retain a molecular memory of their developmental positions in the body. Furthermore, the team used the map as a reference to track how the fish regenerates missing neurons in the forebrain after injury. The complete atlas has been made publicly available through an interactive online resource called DigiFish.

item.title: Velo3D Selected for $10M DEVCOM Armaments Center Award
item.description:
According to TCT Magazine, the US Army DEVCOM Armaments Center selected Velo3D through the ONIX Marketplace under an Other Transaction Authority pathway. This acquisition approach is specifically designed to bridge the gap between commercial innovations and military needs.
Under this potential $10 million program, Velo3D will focus on establishing modular payload architectures, advanced warhead components, and scalable manufacturing. The work will primarily involve Inconel 718—a material already qualified on Velo3D's Sapphire platform—and a second high-performance alloy directed by the government.
While Velo3D handles the additive manufacturing process development, production, and quality documentation, the U.S. government retains design authority and responsibility for lethality testing. A core part of the initiative relies on Velo3D's Golden Print File methodology, which aims to ensure repeatable production quality across different machines and domestic facilities.

item.title: Giga Storage on how European battery asset management is evolving
item.description:
In an interview with Energy-Storage.news, Kathleen Dingenen from Giga Storage discusses the rapid evolution of battery energy storage system (BESS) asset management in Europe. Three years ago, assets were small and relied mostly on frequency containment reserves. Today, grid-scale batteries reach gigawatt-hour proportions, shifting value to wholesale trading and complex revenue stacking.
Key regulatory changes like the EU’s RfG 2.0 are making grid-forming capabilities mandatory for large storage, directly impacting inverter specifications, warranties, and plant operations. Furthermore, asset managers are moving away from rigid daily cycle caps toward annual throughput limits, leveraging LFP chemistry and liquid cooling. However, accurate state-of-charge estimation remains a practical challenge that requires robust buffers and continuous monitoring to prevent revenue losses.

item.title: Clearing Cellular Traffic Jams Treats Multiple Diseases in Mice
item.description:
According to Broad Institute:
According to researchers at the Broad Institute publishing in _Neuron_, a group of over 50 inherited disorders known as proteinopathies share a common root cause: misfolded proteins accumulating inside cells and overwhelming the cellular quality-control machinery.
Building on their previous work on TMED9 in MUC1 kidney disease, the team found that TMED2, 7, 9, and 10 form a protein complex that traps these misfolded proteins and causes a cellular traffic jam. By deleting or targeting a key component of this complex called TMED7, scientists were able to release the trapped proteins to be recycled without disrupting normal cellular functions, successfully reversing disease hallmarks in mice with MUC1 kidney disease and slowing vision loss in a model of retinitis pigmentosa.

item.title: Freiburg team secures about 10 million euros to explore commercial plastic volumetric 3D printing
item.description: Background and Funding According to Nanjixiong, process technology professor Bastian Rapp and interface chemistry and physics professor Jürgen Rühe from the University of Freiburg have secured about 10 million euros in European Research Council (ERC) synergy funding. The funding will support the six-year CHiC2PRINT project, selected from over 950 applications. Technical Approach The project aims to bridge the gap between commercially mature plastics and light-driven additive manufacturing. Instead of traditional layer-by-layer stacking, the team plans to use directed light exposure to form three-dimensional structures inside an existing volume of plastic. By combining process technology and interface chemistry, they aim to make standard plastics responsive to light control. Recycling and Outlook CHiC2PRINT also incorporates product end-of-life handling into its design, aiming to separate formed objects through a process called hierarchical dissociation to recover and reuse raw plastics. The project intends to investigate whether commercial plastic systems can combine complex geometry manufacturing with efficient recycling, though specific recycling rates and production speeds are yet to be established.

item.title: Pinecone now exports cost data in FOCUS format for FinOps tools
item.description: According to Pinecone: Previously, finance teams had to manually download and reshape Pinecone billing files to track cloud costs using FinOps tools. With the new Cost and Usage Export API, available to Enterprise organizations, users can generate exports for any time window over the past year either via the console or the Admin API. The data is provided as FOCUS v1.4 CSV files packed in a zip format, including project and index tags that allow precise chargeback to individual teams or applications. Platform teams can also automate the entire pipeline by scheduling jobs to pull these reports directly into data warehouses.

item.title: Cailabs CEO Discusses Laser Communications and US Plans on Space Minds
item.description:
During an appearance on the SpaceNews podcast *Space Minds* at Space Tech Expo Europe, Cailabs co-founder and CEO Jean-François Morizur joined host Mike Gruss to discuss the evolving landscape of space optical communications. Morizur focused on clearing up industry misconceptions surrounding laser communications technology.
Additionally, the discussion covered Cailabs' ongoing business strategy, including specific plans for the United States market and why establishing standardized interoperability remains a critical priority for future satellite networks.

item.title: Towards a Science of Capable Autonomous Agents & Provable Safety — Part II
item.description: According to Carnegie Mellon ML Blog: In Part II of this series, the author addresses how to ensure capable autonomous agents remain open to human correction, even when intervention conflicts with task completion. Drawing on recent game-theoretic and complexity-theoretic results from AAAI 2026, the author proves that communication costs grow with the number of objectives and that reward hacking is inevitable under finite-sample estimation. To address why standard RLHF or single rewards fail to achieve corrigibility, the research presents sufficient conditions for satisfying corrigibility requirements in partially observable off-switch games by structuring five distinct utility heads with strict priority gaps (deference, switch preservation, truthfulness, low impact, and task reward). Furthermore, the author highlights empirical findings from the ROGUE benchmark, showing that LLM agents often fail to maintain safety constraints during ordinary computer use or delegation. Finally, the paper discusses 'sharding'—dividing evaluation criteria across separate model requests to prevent oversight overload.

item.title: FDA Approves Regeneron's Livsayis as First siRNA Therapy for Generalized Myasthenia Gravis
item.description:
According to Regeneron, the FDA approval of Livsayis marks the company's second new drug modality this year, following the approval of its hearing loss gene therapy in April. Livsayis is a complement component factor 5 (C5)-directed siRNA designed to limit terminal complement activation, which is a major driver of generalized myasthenia gravis, a progressive autoimmune disease causing muscle weakness.
The approval was supported by the Phase 3 NIMBLE trial, in which the therapy showed a statistically significant improvement in daily functioning scores compared to a placebo at 24 weeks. Analysts at Truist Securities and BMO Capital Markets noted that the quarterly dosing schedule provides a practical advantage for the patient experience.
Like other therapies that reduce C5 activity, Livsayis carries a boxed warning for serious meningococcal and other infections, and it will be available exclusively through a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) program.

item.title: Anthropic Hits $2 Trillion Valuation in Nasdaq Debut After Shares Surge 34%
item.description: IPO Performance and Valuation According to Reuters, Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 per share after selling 980 million shares, raising substantial capital ahead of its public debut. When trading began, the stock opened at $111.5, representing a 34% surge over the IPO price and pushing the company's total market capitalization past the $2 trillion threshold. This milestone makes Anthropic the world's first publicly traded frontier AI company, positioning it alongside tech giants like Microsoft, Apple, and Nvidia in the trillion-dollar club. Industry Implications and Market Sentiment Market analysts view this blockbuster debut, alongside Nvidia's recent earnings report, as a crucial test of investor confidence in the AI sector amid ongoing debates over heavy spending and profitability.
